title: SSE snapshot resume indexing and correction procedure
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported truncated or duplicated tokens after transient network disconnects when using the Hosted SSE streaming API. Symptoms included final partial sentences, duplicate fragments after resume, and occasional fragment reordering. This ticket defines a deterministic snapshot/resume indexing contract, short-term mitigations, and a correction service to repair affected transcripts and prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps:
1) Open a long-running streaming session (output > 1024 tokens or >45s) to the hosted SSE endpoint via Node or Python SDK.
2) Induce a transient network disconnect at the edge (TCP RST or proxy restart) during token emission.
3) Reconnect with current SDK resume heuristics (client offset + last_event_id).
4) Observe reconstructed transcript: missing token ranges, exact duplicate fragments, or fragments arriving out of order.
Observed on macOS Node SDK v3.1.2, Python SDK v2.8.1, and raw SSE clients behind edge proxies in us-west1.
root_cause_summary: A mismatch between ephemeral edge buffering/coalescing and server-side in-flight session state. Edge buffers sometimes asynchronously flush or replay fragments while the runtime's in-memory cursor advanced without a durable checkpoint. Resume heuristics that used optimistic client offsets and last_event markers are brittle across proxy coalescing and worker failover, causing missing tokens, duplicated fragments, and rare reordering. There was also no per-fragment checksum or authoritative durable session snapshot persisted outside process memory.
short_term_mitigation:
1) Tweak edge proxy config to reduce aggressive coalescing and enable a conservative graceful-drain before restart.
2) Ship SDK patch that computes per-fragment hashes and performs client-side deduplication and tolerant merges (drop exact duplicates, prefer lower fragment_seq on conflict).
3) Offer per-tenant emergency fallback to non-streaming endpoints for highly impacted customers for 24-72h during rollout.
4) Notify affected customers with an incident summary and expected timeline; provide rollback instructions for critical workloads.
long_term_fix_plan:
1) Persist a canonical per-session snapshot index (snapshot_id + last_committed_sequence_number) to a durable kv with strong write semantics at periodic checkpoints (default every 256 tokens or 5s).
2) Add fragment metadata headers: (session_id, snapshot_id, fragment_seq, payload_length, sha256_fragment_hash) and validate on append.
3) Define deterministic resume handshake: client supplies last_seen_snapshot_id and last_seen_fragment_seq; server responds with an explicit open_resume_range or a continue token; remove implicit heuristics.
4) Build an async backfill and correction service that replays logs between snapshots to produce corrected transcripts and records corrections to an immutable corrections table exposed in Console and API.
5) Update SDKs to implement the new resume contract, checksum verification, and de-duplication logic.
6) Provide a compatibility gateway and migration path for older clients, and schedule an EOL for legacy heuristics after rollout.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for header parsing, checksum verification, and handshake edge cases.
Integration tests simulating reconnects across a simulated edge proxy asserting no missing/duplicate/reordering issues for large synthetic workloads (10k sessions).
Chaos tests with randomized disconnects, proxy restarts, and worker failover.
Regression suite that replays historical incident traces referenced in related_issues.
Canary: enable canonical resume for 1% traffic for 72 hours and monitor telemetry before progressive ramp.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy runtime changes behind a feature flag.
2) Release SDKs with resume handshake and hash validation.
3) Enable feature for internal tenants and run a 1% canary for 72 hours.
4) Ramp to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over one week with rollback gates based on telemetry.
5) Run backfill/correction on known affected sessions after reaching 50% if stable.
6) Deprecate legacy heuristics and announce 60-day EOL for old SDK resume behavior.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Add metrics and alerts: resume_error_rate (tenant) > 0.5% for 30m -> P1; duplicate_fragment_rate spike > baseline + 0.2% -> warn; snapshot_persist_latency p95 > 250ms -> warn; backfill_job_failure_rate > 0% -> P0.
Dashboards: per-tenant resume success ratio, resume reason distribution, corrected transcript counts.
Instrumentation queries: sessions with >1 reconnect and fragment_hash_mismatch; histogram of time delta between last_committed_sequence_number and client last_seen fragment.
Runbook: P0 -> escalate to oncall-engineering -> runtime lead -> infra-sre; enable forced-fallback for impacted tenants if required.
notes: Architecture discussion: evaluated durable kv vs. append-only log; chose kv with CAS for cheap idempotent updates to LCSN. Edge changes coordinated with platform infra to avoid tail-latency regressions. Customer comms template approved by Solutions and Marketing. After rollout, schedule a retrospective to tune checkpoint interval for latency-sensitive tenants.
